response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack software engineer (15+ years) with strong web, backend, and low-latency service work, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect for AI accelerators. There is no evidence of SoC or IP modeling, RTL/architectural simulation, GPU or SIMD/MIMD architecture work, deep-learning training/inference optimization, or hardware-software co-design. The closest adjacencies are C/C++ components at National Instruments, robotics/embedded exposure at Altom, and low-latency D services at Sociomantic — none of which approach principal-level silicon architecture. Education (BS CS) meets the 8+ years bar numerically, but the experience is in an unrelated domain.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering across web, mobile, embedded, and CI/CD
Some low-latency, high-throughput systems work (async I/O, fibers, millions of req/s)
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, open-source ownership, teaching and public talks
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, hardware architecture, or silicon performance analysis experience
No demonstrated deep-learning workload, GPU, or AI-accelerator optimization background
Career trajectory is application/full-stack, not principal-level hardware architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture experience
No AI/deep-learning or GPU workload optimization background
Extensive general software engineering tenure and systems/low-latency exposure
